CVE-2026-120308.title: Beta9 host filesystem exposure via volume path traversal
CVE-2026-120308.description: A Beta9 tenant can attach a volume when deploying a function, endpoint, or task queue. The gateway builds the host path by joining the shared volumes root, the workspace name, and the volume identifier from the stub configuration. Nothing checks that the identifier names a volume that workspace owns. Parent-directory segments in the identifier collapse the joined path to the worker's filesystem root, and the worker bind-mounts that path into the sandbox read-write unless the volume was explicitly marked read-only. A tenant with a workspace token can therefore read and write the worker's files, including other tenants' volumes stored on that machine. Confirmed against gateway 0.1.769 and worker 0.1.745. Fixed in gateway 0.1.776 and worker 0.1.756: volume identifiers and mount paths are validated before a mount is built, including for stubs saved before the check existed, and the gateway rejects a volume that does not exist or is not owned by the workspace.

CVE-2026-133429.title: Validation bypass of extra data keys in JSON model validation
CVE-2026-133429.description:
When validating JSON data into a model allowing extra data, the keys of extra data aren't validated against the key type annotated on __pydantic_extra__, resulting in extra data not matching the declared type. This is the case if you define __pydantic_extra__ as e.g. dict[Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r'^x_')], int].

The validate_json_by_iteration() method (in pydantic-core/src/validators/model_fields.rs), used to validate JSON data into models, only validates the values of extra data, and stores the keys as is.

The issue was fixed in commit 4c65dbda9970a488e2ff21c8693fc6f6d70a3358.

Impact: validation bypass, as extra data returned by validation doesn't match the declared type. Affected are applications validating untrusted JSON data into models allowing extra data (with extra='allow'), with a key type annotated on __pydantic_extra__ (e.g. dict[Annotated[str, Field(pattern=...)], int]), using Pydantic from 2.13.0 up to (but excluding) 2.14.2.

Python mode validation isn't affected.
